sections.skill: Read negations, units and relationships exactly as stated

questions.prompt: Three students each make one statement about themself, and every statement is true. Dee: "It is not true that I finished the race." Eli: "I did not fail to finish the race." Fay: "I never said that I finished the race." Who definitely finished the race?

Shoelaces are sold only in packs of 2 laces for $3 a pack. Each sneaker needs exactly one lace. A club needs laces for 12 sneakers and also buys 4 whistles at $5 each. What is the least the club can spend, in dollars?
The Ortiz family has at least one son and at least one daughter. Each son has exactly one brother, and each daughter has exactly two brothers and three sisters. How many children are in the family?
A box holds only red pens and blue pens: at least 3 red pens, at most 2 blue pens, and exactly 6 pens in all. Which statement MUST be true?

choices.text: There are at least 4 red pens.

questions.correct_answer: There are at least 4 red pens.

questions.prompt: On this team, April, June and May are the names of three players (not months). A coach writes: "June scored after April and before May." Put the players in the order in which they scored, first to last.

sections.skill: Strategy: rewrite each statement in plain form
sections.relationship: Students who miss MAIN usually react to the first impression of a sentence. Rewriting each statement in plain form (cancel double negatives, convert units, turn "at least" into a number list) removes the trap.
sections.author_note: Students who miss MAIN usually react to the first impression of a sentence. Rewriting each statement in plain form (cancel double negatives, convert units, turn "at least" into a number list) removes the trap.

lesson.title: Rewrite each statement in plain form
text: Before solving, rewrite every statement so that it says one plain thing.
Double negatives cancel: "not untrue" means "true", and "did not fail to" means "did".
Units: decide whether a number counts items or groups (pairs, packs, dozens) and convert.
"At least 3" means 3, 4, 5, ...; "at most 3" means 0, 1, 2 or 3. List the values that are still possible.
A sentence about what someone SAID or THINKS is not a fact about the world.

example.title: Worked example (a different situation)
prompt: "It is not untrue that the library is not open." Is the library open?
Eggs come in cartons of a dozen. Pia needs 30 eggs. How many cartons must she buy?
steps: "Not untrue" means "true", so the sentence says: the library is not open.
Cartons hold 12 eggs. 2 cartons give 24 eggs, which is too few; 3 cartons give 36, which is enough. She must buy 3 cartons.

questions.prompt: Treat "unhappy" as meaning exactly "not happy". What does "Rui is not unhappy" say?
A drawer holds 18 single socks that make complete matching pairs. How many pairs is that?
"At most 3 people may enter" allows exactly 3 people to enter.
"Not all of the doors are locked." Which statement means the same?

choices.text: At least one door is unlocked.

questions.correct_answer: At least one door is unlocked.

sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: Four statements: (1) "It is not the case that 7 is not odd." (2) "It is false that 10 is not even." (3) "It is not true that 9 is not a multiple of 4." (4) "5 is not unequal to 5." How many of the four statements are true?

On a quiz show, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday are the first names of four contestants. The host says: "Wednesday answered before Monday. Friday answered right after Tuesday. Monday did not answer last." Put the contestants in answering order, first to last.

A bag holds only red and blue marbles: the number of red marbles is at least twice the number of blue, there are at least 3 blue marbles, and there are at most 10 marbles in all. Give a possible number of red marbles r and blue marbles b.
questions.rule: r >= 2*b and b >= 3 and r + b <= 10 and isInteger(r) and isInteger(b)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: r >= 2*b and b >= 3 and r + b <= 10 and isInteger(r) and isInteger(b) (example: r = 6, b = 3)

questions.prompt: In a group of brothers and sisters, every girl has exactly as many brothers as sisters, and there are 3 boys. How many girls are there?
"No student who did not study passed the test." Which statement follows?
